description: Open source previs software in the browser: block a scene, pose characters, author camera moves and cuts, then take the same shots to an AI video model.

latest_release.name: CozyClay v3.2.3
latest_release.body:
Install without a terminal on Windows and macOS, a dark Studio with a guided first visit, Auto Pose, camera roll and per-part motion keys, plus cast and stability fixes.

Install

- On Windows the Install dialog leads with one download, `CozyClay-Setup.exe`;
  the Node.js and terminal steps stay one click away. (#1188)
- On macOS the Install dialog leads with one download, `CozyClay.dmg`: a
  signed, notarized app that opens the Studio in its own window, with no
  Terminal. `cozyclay.org/install.sh` stays for a one-line install. (#1190)
- The landing page has one Install action; its dialog asks which computer the
  Studio goes on. Phones are not offered Install. (#1281, #1189)
- An install that starts in the hosted Studio says `--via playground`, and an
  installer start keeps its `installer` label on first launch. (#1183, #1258)

Studio

- The Studio starts in the dark theme. A theme already chosen in Preferences
  is kept. (#1163)
- A first visit to the hosted Studio opens on a ready stage with a character
  on it, then the eight-step camera tutorial in English, 한국어 or 简体中文.
  `npx cozyclay` keeps the project chooser. (#1159, #1161)
- Sample motions in the Motion tab: one click installs a walk or a flip on the
  selected character and plays it, with no agent. (#1156)
- Fix and tell, Annotate, pose keys, lying poses and a more compact shell.
  (#1131)
- The Auto Pose tool. (#1257)
- Import a character file on another rig and play it on its own bones. (#1150)
- A large world scale for full-size exterior scenes. (#1143)
- A smaller gizmo, a repaired Add menu, and a narrow Studio, HUD and install
  commands that stay usable. (#1182, #1264)

Camera

- Roll the shot camera about its lens axis. (#1144)
- Record mouse aim while the rail plays. (#1262)
- Rail readouts stay in sync with the rendered camera. (#1265)

Motion

- Keys are fixed per body part and merge, the Plan card folds, and the beat
  board is gone. (#1219)
- The v4 motion engine, on CozyClay's agent loop and on Claude Code, as
  opt-in Studio Agent models; body motion runs as a motion task designed
  first. (#1134, #1138)
- Rig templates compile specs on non-Mixamo rigs; flight physics with FLOAT,
  DROP and SPIN checks; `fix.self` repairs arms through the body. (#1148,
  #1149, #1154)
- QA measures fingers, palms, knees and torso against the floor and objects,
  and stops at the first take a viewer would accept; trivial spec slips are
  corrected instead of refusing the spec. (#1113, #1114, #1126)

Agent

- A task card names the model it runs on. (#1165)
- A visible thing is built as one detailed sculpt, looked at and copied.
  (#1169)
- On the hosted Studio the Agent panel shows four ready-made requests and an
  Install button instead of a server error. (#1156)
- The generation prompt describes every visible character, keeps the real
  aspect ratio, and no longer invents a location or look. (#1213, #1238)
- Tool descriptions and prompts match the code. (#1228, #1239)

Export

- Choose the video export's pixel size. (#1145)

Cast and shots

- Every cast member keeps a stable identity; shots persist and follow the
  named cast and frame groups. (#1244)
- A character whose model fails to load falls back to the proxy figure, and
  aborted model loads recover. (#1197, #1284)

Fixes

- Opening a project normalizes stored objects instead of throwing; save
  records a written file as saved. (#1196, #1207)
- A task that touched more than 100 objects finishes normally; an edit no
  longer rebuilds every sculpt. (#1167, #1168)
- Fixed a Pin-tool scrub update loop and uncaught pointer and sculpt errors.
  (#1195, #1186)
- The unfinished Workflow entry points are hidden. (#1211)

Site

- The hosted Studio (`cozyclay.org/app/`) records masked PostHog session
  replays: inputs and the agent transcript are masked, the 3D viewport is
  sampled at 2 fps, and no console logs or network contents are kept. The
  landing page and the npm package never record. The privacy page says so.

detail.readme:
Make the scene first. Then make it a video.
Open source previs in a browser tab: block the set, move the cast, cut the camera, hand the shot to an AI video model.

Try it in the browser · Quick start · Guide for AI agents · Docs · Changelog · Discord

Top: the greybox blocked in CozyClay. Bottom: the AI video made from it. Same idea, a parkour jump: the blocking holds the timing and the camera.
## Why AI video costs money per take, and one miss means paying again. A text prompt cannot hold a whole scene: where everyone stands, how they move, where the camera is, when it cuts. CozyClay lets you make those decisions first, in 3D, where they are cheap to change. Then the video model gets the shot as a first frame, a greybox reference clip and a prompt that describes the real framing. It follows the blocking instead of guessing. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["Stage
set + cast"] --> M["Motion
compiled + QA"] --> C["Camera
shots + cuts"] --> E["Export
frame · clip · prompt"] --> V["AI video model"] ``` ## Quick start ```bash npx cozyclay ``` That is the whole install. You need Node.js 22.19 or newer and a Chromium browser. You do not need a GPU, Python or a model download. The studio opens at `http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/`. **Updating.** `npx cozyclay` fetches the newest release each time you run it. After `npm install -g cozyclay`, the studio shows a small **Update** chip in the top bar when a newer release is out. **Update now** installs it, and **Restart now** starts the new version in the same terminal; the studio reloads once your project is saved. On Windows the chip gives you the command to copy instead: one-click stays off there by design. `cclay update` does the same from the terminal. `--no-update-check` or `COZYCLAY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` turns the check off for one launch; `cclay update --off` turns it off for good, and `cclay update --on` brings it back. > **Asking an AI agent to set it up?** Give it this repository link. Its instructions are in > [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md). ## What you can do | | | | --- | --- | | **Stage** | Build the set from primitives. Add rigged characters, or capsule stand-ins when nobody needs to move a limb. Fly the view like a 3D editor. | | **Move** | Describe the action. The agent writes a motion spec, and a deterministic compiler in the browser bakes every frame. QA checks collisions, foot slide, reach and hand contact before you see it. | | **Shoot** | Put shots on a timeline, draw dolly rails, look through the lens. Each shot knows the limits of the video model you target. | | **Export** | Keyframe pack (first and last frame, greybox clip, camera, prompt), mp4, depth and normal passes, contact sheet, OTIO cut list. | | **Storyboard** | Prefer stills? A Storyboard project is a row of panels with captions, an animatic and a contact sheet. | | **Undo anything** | Every edit, including each change the agent makes, is one undo step. | ## Direct it with AI The same scene can be driven from three places, live, while you watch the viewport. | Surface | Start | For | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent panel** | `Cmd/Ctrl+B` in the studio | Chat in the studio. Sign in with ChatGPT or use your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, MiniMax, OpenRouter, CLIProxyAPI). | | **MCP server** | `npx -y cozyclay mcp` | Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client. | | **Terminal** | `cclay live status --wait` | Coding agents that drive a running studio, JSON in and out. | ```json { "mcpServers": { "cozyclay": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "cozyclay", "mcp"] } } } ``` ## From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/HaD0Yun/CozyClay.git && cd CozyClay npm install npm run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5180/app/ npm test ``` ## Docs | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [`INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) | Install, run and connect, written for AI agents | | [`docs/motion3-agent-guide.md`](docs/motion3-agent-guide.md) | Motion specs, compile and QA | | [`docs/agent-cli.md`](docs/agent-cli.md) | `cclay live`, model providers, sessions | | [`mcp/README.md`](mcp/README.md) | MCP tools and the live protocol | | [`docs/studio-ui-ia.md`](docs/studio-ui-ia.md) | Every control and where it lives | | [`docs/privacy.md`](docs/privacy.md) | Anonymous telemetry and how to turn it off (`cclay telemetry off`) | | [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) | Contribution rules | ## Guides | Read | For | | --- | --- | | [Greybox to AI video](https://cozyclay.org/greybox-to-video/) | Why a grey blockout is the most reliable input for a video model, and the block-then-generate loop | | [Previs software compared](https://cozyclay.org/previs-software/) | Free, open source and browser-based previs tools side by side | | [Seedance 2.5 camera control](https://cozyclay.org/seedance-camera-control/) | Getting the same camera on every take with a reference clip | | [Camera control for AI video](https://cozyclay.org/ai-camera-control/) | Why camera prompts drift and what the models actually accept | Found a bug or want a feature? [Open an issue](https://github.com/HaD0Yun/CozyClay/issues). ## License AGPL-3.0-or-later.
